sections.title: Technologies your guides only touch

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: You do not need these all in depth. Know what each is for and when you would refuse to use it; go deeper only if a job description asks.

blocks.title: Mono is 0 or 1 item; Flux is many

blocks.caption: Since Java 21, virtual threads remove much of the reason to go reactive just for concurrency.

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: One blocking call on a WebFlux event-loop thread stalls many requests. Blocking JDBC does not belong there.

sections.title: Spring Batch
blocks: For large, restartable jobs such as nightly settlements: a **Job** has **Steps**; a chunk step reads, processes and writes N items per transaction. Its job repository records progress, so a failed run restarts where it stopped. Prefer it over a hand-written `@Scheduled` loop when volume or restartability matters.

sections.title: GraphQL
blocks: The client asks for exactly the fields it wants from one endpoint. It suits varied clients and aggregating several sources. The costs: harder HTTP caching, query-cost limits are needed, and N+1 calls unless you batch (`@BatchMapping` in Spring for GraphQL).

rows: Public or simple APIs, cacheable resources
Many client shapes, an aggregation layer

sections.title: Load testing
blocks: k6, Gatling and JMeter generate realistic traffic. Test at the expected load, then find the breaking point, and watch **p95 and p99**, not averages. Generate load from a separate machine, use production-like data, and warm up the JVM first. Your numbers then have a defensible source for your resume.

blocks.title: A k6 script
Key points
blocks.text:
- Virtual threads cover most concurrency needs without reactive code.
- Spring Batch for large restartable jobs.
- REST by default; GraphQL and gRPC for specific reasons.
- Measure p95 and p99, on realistic data.

items.question: Why not rewrite a Spring MVC service in WebFlux for scale?
items.answer: With blocking JDBC there is little gain, and the code gets harder to debug. Virtual threads usually give the throughput with simpler code.

items.question: Why is average latency a poor load-test metric?
items.answer: It hides the slow tail that real users hit. Report p95 and p99 along with the error rate.
